title: ESP32 JTAG debugging: breakpoints and watchpoints

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “ESP32 JTAG debugging: breakpoints and watchpoints” correctly?
options: A USB-C connector does not mean the chip supports USB HID.
JTAG lets a debugger halt real ESP32 hardware, step through source lines, and inspect variables and memory.
A Hall sensor detects magnetic fields.
Many ESP32 boards have no built-in RGB LED.
questions.answer: JTAG lets a debugger halt real ESP32 hardware, step through source lines, and inspect variables and memory.
questions.explanation: JTAG lets a debugger halt real ESP32 hardware, step through source lines, and inspect variables and memory.

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “ESP32 JTAG debugging: breakpoints and watchpoints” is accurate?
options: Some boards use a USB-to-serial bridge only for flashing.
Older original ESP32 chips had an internal Hall sensor and legacy APIs
Where present, the LED may be addressable or a discrete RGB part with different pin/driver wiring.
OpenOCD bridges the target to GDB.
questions.answer: OpenOCD bridges the target to GDB.
questions.explanation: OpenOCD bridges the target to GDB.

questions.prompt: Which practical detail should be considered when using “ESP32 JTAG debugging: breakpoints and watchpoints”?
options: Certain ESP32-S2/S3 boards with native USB OTG can expose CDC and HID
Set a breakpoint or watchpoint on `sampleCount`
families such as ESP32-S2/S3/C3 do not have the same integrated sensor.
`RGB_BUILTIN` and `rgbLedWrite` require a supporting Arduino-ESP32 version and board.
questions.answer: Set a breakpoint or watchpoint on `sampleCount`
questions.explanation: Set a breakpoint or watchpoint on `sampleCount`

questions.prompt: Which statement from the “ESP32 JTAG debugging: breakpoints and watchpoints” lesson is correct?
options: verify the exact board and Arduino core configuration.
the one-second delay keeps the task from busy-spinning.
